item.title: Alonso to lead Aston Martin in Dakar Rally bid
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Spanish Formula One driver Fernando Alonso of team Aston Martin speaks to the media at the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace in São Paulo, ahead of the São Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday. (is associated with: «Alonso to lead Aston Martin in Dakar Rally bid») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Formula One driver Fernando Alonso is ready to “embrace the challenge” as he returns to the Dakar Rally in January for the first time in seven years. The 45-year-old will lead Aston Martin’s first entry into the famous event, alongside nine-time world rally champion Sebastien Loeb and reigning champion Lucas Moraes. Alonso, the double F1 champion who recently signed a new deal to remain in the sport with Aston Martin, said in a statement on Tuesday: “Formula One remains my priority. But I am a racing driver, and challenges like this are why I love competing. I’m looking forward to seeing what we can achieve. “In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both Formula One and the Dakar Rally in the same year.” The Dakar Rally takes place in Portugal and Morocco January 9-23. F1 testing for the new season is scheduled from February 24.

item.title: Rob Gronkowski sends A.J. Brown message as Patriots trade disappointment grows
item.description: Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images Rob Gronkowski has admitted that the New England Patriots’ decision to trade for A.J. Brown has been a disappointment so far, although he remains hopeful the wide receiver can turn things around. The Patriots sent Philadelphia a 2028 first-round pick and a conditional 2027 fifth-round selection to bring Brown to New England in the offseason. However, the former Eagles star has struggled to stay healthy and has featured in just four of the Patriots’ first 10 games. His latest setback came during New England’s 35-10 defeat to the Detroit Lions, leaving the team at 5-5. Rob Gronkowski backs A.J. Brown despite disappointment with Patriots trade Speaking on the Gronk & Jules Show alongside former teammate Julian Edelman, Gronkowski did not hide his frustration with how the move has worked out. “I don’t know what’s going on with his situation, but I’m cheering for A.J. Brown to get back on the right path because, so far, I mean, I don’t even want to say it, because he’s been such a great player, but it’s been a disappointment, you know, the disappointing trade so far. First-rounder, he just hasn’t lived up to the hype.” Gronkowski was keen to stress that he still believes Brown can make a difference once he gets back to full fitness. The wide receiver returned from a knee injury against Detroit but suffered a hamstring problem after catching a 21-yard pass. He did not return and finished with two catches for 27 yards on six targets. It was another frustrating chapter in a difficult first season. Brown previously missed time with an ankle sprain and knee issue, leaving him with just 11 receptions for 128 yards and no touchdowns. New England now has its bye week before travelling to face the Los Angeles Chargers, giving Brown time to recover. The Patriots need their major offseason acquisition back on the field. With New England sitting at 5-5 after consecutive defeats, Mike Vrabel will hope Brown can finally deliver the impact expected when the club surrendered a first-round pick to acquire him. item.title: Roma chase next Malen as they target unhappy Chelsea and Forest wingers
item.description: Roma chase next Malen as they target unhappy Chelsea and Forest wingers Il Corriere dello Sport reports that Roma are closely monitoring Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Nottingham Forest’s Callum Hudson-Odoi, hoping that a new attacking signing from the Premier League will have the same impact as Donyell Malen. Roma are still looking for attacking reinforcement, specifically, a left winger. According to Corriere dello Sport, two of the primary names for the Giallorossi are Chelsea’s Gittens and Forest’s Hudson-Odoi. Roma look to Chelsea and Forest for the next Malen HONG KONG, CHINA – AUGUST 5: Jamie Gittens of Chelsea FC reacts during the preseason friendly between Chelsea and Juventus at the Kai Tak Stadium on August 5, 2026 in Hong Kong, China. (Photo by Yu Chun Christopher Wong/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images) Both English wingers seem to be in a similar situation: unhappy with the lack of playing time at their clubs and looking for a fresh start in the January window. This is not the first time Gittens has been linked with a move to Roma, as the Giallorossi already held talks with Chelsea last summer. The 22-year-old has played just 55 minutes across all competitions and is recovering from an ankle injury that has kept him sidelined for over a month. According to the report, Roma and Chelsea have stayed in contact in recent weeks, and talks could intensify soon if Roma receive guarantees about the player’s fitness. BRIGHTON, ENGLAND – MARCH 29: Callum Hudson-Odoi of Nottingham Forest during the Emirates FA Cup Quarter Final match between Brighton & Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest at Amex Stadium on March 29, 2025 in Brighton, England. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Hudson-Odoi has only played 45 minutes in the Premier League this season, making just four league appearances. According to the report, the 26-year-old is open to a move to the Olimpico in the January window. Barely one year ago, in January 2026, Roma signed Malen from Aston Villa on an initial loan deal with an option to buy. Back then, the Dutchman was looking to revive his career after an inconsistent spell at Aston Villa, and his 27 goals in 34 Roma appearances prove he succeeded. Roma hope to achieve the same with a new attacking signing from the Premier League during the 2027 January transfer window.

item.title: Gerrard backs Pochettino appointment at Manchester United but warns a revival will take time
item.description: Gerrard backs Pochettino appointment at Manchester United but warns a revival will take time Steven Gerrard believes Mauricio Pochettino is the right appointment for Manchester United but warned it will take time to revive the club's fortunes. Pochettino will take official charge of Manchester United tomorrow, after the Red Devils moved to appoint the Argentine as Michael Carrick's successor. Pochettino returns to the Premier League after previous spells with Southampton, Spurs, and Chelsea, and arrives after a recent spell in charge of the United States national team. The 54-year-old is tasked with turning around Manchester United's worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with the club in the relegation places after 10 games. Asked about the appointment, Gerrard told The Overlap Daily that Pochettino has the credentials to succeed at Old Trafford. He pointed to Pochettino's popular status at former clubs as a good sign that he can win over the dressing room. Gerrard tips Pochettino to win over United’s dressing room: “Players like to work for him” "I think it's the right appointment. I've been a fan of Pochettino in terms of Tottenham, Chelsea, and the job he's done with the USA. I'm a big fan of him, in terms of his style. I think he would have been on their list for a long time, so they would have admired him for a long time," Gerrard said. "His style probably matches the style they want on a consistent basis, in terms of that high energy, front-foot, intense style of play. That's what he brought to Tottenham. That's what we saw at Chelsea for small periods. That's why the USA have appointed him. "He's a really good man manager. Players like to work for him. You listen to all the interviews when he left Spurs, your Harry Kanes, Dele Allis, Kyle Walkers, they all loved him. If he can hit the ground running at United you can see it being a real positive appointment." Gerrard was asked how long he thinks it will take Pochettino to improve United's fortunes, and warned there will be no quick fix. He said the first challenge will be to make Manchester United difficult to beat, having conceded 30 goals across all competitions this season - a joint-high across Europe's top-five leagues. "I think eventually you will see what his philosophy has been for a long time, which is fast, intense, attacking football. He's an elite manager in my opinion. From what I've seen of this Manchester United group, we need to see a little bit more of a pragmatic Manchester United. "You look at the amount of goals they've conceded and where they are sitting in the league. I'm not sure Poch is going to be able to come in and say we're going to play this attacking, energetic, fast-flowing football. I don't think that's going to happen from the off. "He's going to have to stiffen them up. He's going to have to find a structure. He's going to have to get them to run more, and defend better and fight more."

item.title: Report card from Nebraska’s crucial 31-0 win over Rutgers
item.description: Nebraska snapped its four-game losing streak this past weekend, shutting out Rutgers, 31-0. This not only earned the Huskers bowl eligibility for the third consecutive season but also marked the team's first conference shutout win in over two decades. Though the Scarlet Knights were dealing with a slew of injuries, Nebraska's struggles heading into the game presented a crucial matchup. A few injuries on the Huskers' roster also presented opportunities for Rutgers. But in the end, Nebraska fought hard and got the win. That said, the Huskers still have some wrinkles to iron out. Here is the report card from Nebraska’s crucial 31-0 win over Rutgers. Quarterback: B+ Anthony Colandrea looked comfortable against Rutgers, despite limited air time. The Huskers' heavy run game kept Colandrea to just 22 pass attempts, his second-lowest total in a game this season. But he still did a lot on the ground and in the air. Colandrea threw 15-of-22 for 188 yards, averaging over 10 yards per completion for the first time since the Indiana game. He also picked up two touchdown passes, his first multi-touchdown-pass game since Maryland. Colandrea also scored a rushing touchdown, adding to the 66 yards he gained on nine carries. Whether designed or improvised, Colandrea's run looked more decisive here than in past weeks. The run game also let him be more dangerous in the air, catching Rutgers off guard at times and hitting big plays. However, not every pass was perfect. Colandrea just put a ball off target for Barney in the endzone, didn't execute screen passes properly and took a few deep shots that were dangerous. If he cleans that up, this offense can keep moving in the right direction. Colandrea did what was needed for Nebraska in this game, putting the ball on the ground when necessary. However, these final two weeks is going to require more than that. Whether the offense continues to lean on the run or starts implementing more passing plays, Colandrea needs to continue making the most of his plays. The Huskers controlled the game on the ground. However, Nebraska also drained over nine minutes off the clock on its opening drive due to the run game. item.title: Liverpool injury boost as Hungary boss Marco Rossi issues definitive Dominik Szoboszlai update ahead of Manchester United clash
item.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Liverpool have been handed a major boost ahead of their upcoming clash with Manchester United following a positive injury update regarding Dominik Szoboszlai. Despite concerns over a knee problem picked up during domestic duty, the midfielder’s national team manager has moved to allay fears regarding his availability. Rossi clears Szoboszlai despite recent knee scare Marco Rossi declared on Monday that Szoboszlai is injury-free ahead of Hungary's final Nations League group fixture. The national team boss insisted the 26-year-old midfielder is ready to feature despite recent discomfort. Concerns emerged at Selhurst Park, where heavy strapping helped the Liverpool star reach the 69th minute of a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace before he was withdrawn. Although he joined Hungary's squad, the problem resurfaced during Saturday's warm-up in Tbilisi, yet he still started and assisted in a 2-0 win against Georgia. Hungary boss and midfielder address fitness concerns Speaking at Monday's pre-match press conference, Rossi dismissed suggestions that the knee issue affected his captain against Georgia. "Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?" he said. "I didn’t see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available. I don’t think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don’t think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia." Szoboszlai had earlier admitted after Saturday's victory that he nearly pulled out before kick-off after feeling pain while shooting. "I came today with a workout and a half in my legs," he said. "During the warm-up I was close to saying no, because I felt my leg on one of the shots. But if I've come this far, I won't let the team down. I went as best I could, trying to give my best." Club-versus-country friction over injured stars Rossi's stance contrasts sharply with the mood on Merseyside, sparking friction between club and country . Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola had urged caution over the midfielder's Nations League involvement after previous international breaks left his squad depleted. "The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games. Last time, we lost three very important players," he said. "It's the last thing we need, so I hope he can take care of it. item.title: Body of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in Sydney skip
item.description: So You Are competing in the Melbourne Cup at Flemington Racecourse on 3 November [Getty Images] The body of a top Australian racehorse has been found dumped in a skip bin, hours after its trainer revealed the horse had died from colic. In a video shared online, only two weeks after So You Are raced in the Melbourne Cup, the deceased racehorse appeared to be lying in a large metal bin surrounded by other household rubbish in Sydney. Trainer Bjorn Baker - who shared news of the horse's death from colic on Monday - has said he was "deeply distressed" by the video, and called for a "full explanation". Racing NSW, the state's industry regulator, said a preliminary investigation had found the horse was later properly buried, but called the way its body was handled "completely unacceptable". "Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains," Baker said in an statement shared online. "He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death." So You Are had a successful run during spring, winning four times at respected races including the Rosehill, Randwick and the Bendigo Cup. The five-year-old recently finished eight in the Melbourne Cup, which was won by Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles III. The racehorse had received urgent treatment after a severe bout of colic, but was "unfortunately unable to be saved" and was euthanised under anaesthesia, Racing NSW said. "So You Are was then transported for burial, and was being held temporarily, awaiting burial, when these images were recorded," it said. Burial at a licensed landfill is typically recommended for animals that die from euthanasia due to the chemicals involved in the process, according to the racing body. "That burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner," it added. In a statement, REC Equine Specialists - the hospital where the horse died - said a contractor had been hired to dispose of the So You Are's body. "We did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that." "We have spoken with So You Are's owners and trainer to apologise personally." The company added that it had stopped using the contractor, and was reviewing its processes to make sure they known exactly how horses are handled after leaving their hospital. "No owner should have to go through what So You Are's connections have experienced this week. We will make sure it does not happen again." Jowett's video appeared to be filmed at a public rubbish drop-off and land facility called Lucas Heights, in Sutherland Shire, south of Sydney. The waste management company that runs the landfill site said So You Are's body had been moved to a skip bin in a permitted area, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation has reported. item.title: The WTA Finals’ future is bright – but can it ever be ‘the Super Bowl of women’s sports’?
item.description: As 19-year-old Mirra Andreeva beamed and lifted aloft the WTA Finals trophy after a stunning unbeaten run in which she did not drop a set, WTA chair Valerie Camillo could similarly reflect on a job well done. The flagship tournament of the women’s tour, bringing together the eight best players in the world – this year all grand slam winners or finalists, or WTA 1000 champions – has often felt like an afterthought in recent years. But this reset edition in Indian Wells felt like a moment of course-correction – and the signs for the future are largely bright. The last few years have been turbulent for the WTA: the Telegraph reported in September that it could run out of money entirely by next autumn. To condense a long story: the Covid-19 pandemic hit the tour hard, given it held nine significant events in China, including – after signing a 10-year, nearly $1bn deal – the Finals in Shenzhen . The WTA, under Steve Simon, then suspended all events in China over the Peng Shuai scandal, before it was forced into a humiliating climbdown nearly a year and a half later – by which point China pulled the plug on the Shenzhen deal. So the WTA’s biggest tournament, pitting the best athletes against each other, has endured a nomadic, ramshackle existence since then. A last-minute event in Guadalajara in 2021 was followed by a similarly short-notice edition in Fort Worth, Texas the following year, which was poorly promoted and suffered from low ticket sales. Then followed a truly farcical edition in Cancun, where gale force winds and torrential downpour, coupled with hastily-assembled courts and infrastructure players worried was unsafe, made a mockery of the entire thing. The WTA’s three-year partnership with Saudi Arabia brought the prize money to an astonishing high of $15m and gave it a slightly more permanent home. But it always left a sour taste, bringing the pinnacle of women’s sport, and a sport with as long and proud history of trailblazing for gender equality as tennis, to a country with one of the poorest human rights records in the world. (Amnesty International’s April 2026 report into ‘The State of the World’s Human Rights’ detailed how in 2025 the Saudi government “executed the highest number of people on record in any given year” and “severely restricted the rights to freedom of expression and association”, while women “continued to face discrimination in law and practice” and a law passed in 2022 “codified gender-based discrimination in most areas of family life, including in marriage, divorce, child custody and inheritance”.) WTA chair Valerie Camillo attended the trophy ceremony alongside Billie Jean King (Getty) From a purely commercial viewpoint, the Finals in Riyadh was under-promoted and ill-attended and ultimately ended after just two years, with the Saudis scaling back their sporting investments and war in the Middle East bringing yet more uncertainty to the event - a painful end to a high-risk and ultimately reputation-sullying experime

item.title: “Incredible Disrespect Shown”, “Disappointed” – Fans Question ATP Leadership After CEO and Chairman Miss Doubles No. 1 Trophy Ceremony at ATP Finals
item.description: Henry Patten (left) and Harri Heliovaara (right) celebrate their year-end ATP No. 1 trophy for 2026 © Instagram/atptour Several tennis fans questioned Andrea Gaudenzi, the ATP chairman, and Eno Polo, the ATP CEO, over their absence during the trophy presentation for the year-end men’s doubles World No. 1 at the ongoing ATP Finals in Turin, Italy. The trophy went to Henry Patten of Great Britain and Harri Heliovaara of Finland, who had won five titles earlier this year, including the Wimbledon Championships. On Monday, November 16, Patten and Heliovaara received the trophy from Andre Silva, the ATP’s chief tour officer. While delivering his speech, Patten was critical of Gaudenzi and Polo’s absence, saying: “I never would have dreamt that we would be in the position that we’re in now. For us it’s a really big deal. It’s a real shame that the ATP ‌chairman ⁠and the ATP CEO don’t think the same. It would have been nice to have them on court with us ⁠today, but here we are by ourselves.” Subsequently, many fans on X (formerly Twitter) echoed Patten’s sentiments and called out the ATP’s top leadership. One fan wrote: “Fair play Henry – incredible disrespect shown by the ATP higher-ups” Another added: “Incredible bad from the @atptour, Disappointed!” ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi was present at the No. 1 Club Gala ahead of the 2026 ATP Finals On Friday, November 13, the ATP No. 1 Club Gala took place in Turin. The event celebrated all the men’s singles players who, over the years, have reached the No. 1 spot in the ATP Tour rankings. Not every former No. 1 was present, but reigning No. 1 Alexander Zverev, Daniil Medvedev, Jannik Sinner, and past greats such as Stefan Edberg, Marat Safin, Lleyton Hewitt, Juan Carlos Ferrero, and others graced the occasion. The event was opened by Andrea Gaudenzi, the ATP chairman. Gaudenzi was also present for the year-end No. 1 trophy presentation ceremony for Zverev at the Paris Masters , making his absence from the doubles ceremony all the more glaring and contentious. In any case, action at the 2026 ATP Finals has already started, with the year-end tournament set to conclude on Sunday, November 22. item.title: ‘What are you doing?’ – Shannon Sharpe slams Baltimore Ravens for major trade mistake
item.description: Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens’ season is quickly slipping away after they suffered a fifth consecutive defeat against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night. Baltimore lost 23-20 at home despite facing a team that had not won any of their previous eight games. The Ravens have been without Lamar Jackson throughout their losing run after he suffered a thumb injury, while backup Tyler Huntley has also been sidelined with a toe problem. Third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano started two of those games before Baltimore brought in Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett struggled against the Chargers, with no touchdowns and one interception. However, Baltimore’s problems go beyond the quarterback. Their offensive line has been a major weakness, and former Ravens player Shannon Sharpe believes they should already be looking towards next year’s draft. Speaking on Nightcap, Sharpe urged Baltimore to target a high draft pick and use it to strengthen the offensive line. He also questioned why they had not done more to pursue Quenton Nelson before the Indianapolis Colts traded him to the Seattle Seahawks . “What are you doing? Go ahead and try to get yourself a high draft pick,” Sharpe said. “It needs to be an offensive lineman. I don’t know who’s ranked the highest. They need offensive linemen badly. “They should have given up whatever Indy was asking for to get Quenton Nelson. It’s bad. But enough of that. They’ve got my blood pressure up.” Sharpe clearly believes Baltimore missed a major opportunity to address one of their biggest weaknesses. With five straight defeats and their season falling apart, the Ravens may have some difficult decisions to make. item.title: CFP bracket prediction leads college football bowl projections with two weeks left
item.description: It's seems things are becoming clearer in the College Football Playoff race. There are several teams have effectively plan for being in the postseason 12-team field without a meltdown as an overwhelming favorite in the final two weeks. Georgia leads the list that includes Utah, Notre Dame, Alabama and Miami. Boise State looks to have a clear path to the Group of Six berth if it can simply win the Mountain West. That leaves six spots up for grabs. UCLA, Indiana, Texas, Tennessee and Wake Forest all are significant favorites to navigate their respective stretch runs. In the case of the unbeaten Bruins , they likely can survive one loss to either Michigan or Southern California but could be in a dicey situation if they lose both. The others don't want to lose and test the committee further picking apart their credentials. So if those five can survive, the last spot is where things get interesting. Texas Tech would appear to have the inside track by virtue of their ranking from last week that preceded an impressive defeat of Oklahoma State. But there's the matter of a game at Baylor this week that could trip them up. Brigham Young would be the team mostly likely to benefit from a Texas Tech loss with its win against Notre Dame an important card in its hand. Iowa is the other contender lurking in case there is chaos. Another wild card would be Ohio State if the Buckeyes can win out and get an Indiana loss this week that would put them in the Big Ten title game. While this might seem straightforward, history has shown that the field College Football Playoff field can look very different than what it seems with two weeks left in the regular season. So let's see how it all shakes out. item.title: Tigers prospect Maddox Long proves 'pitching can come from anywhere'
item.description: Detroit Tigers pitching prospect Maddox Long delivered a dominant performance in the Arizona Fall League , proving that he is somebody to keep an eye on. “It's a tough assignment going to the Fall League, especially pitching in that environment with the balls and the sun and how it flies and all of that stuff, the quality of position player talent that gets there,” Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris said last week at the GM meetings in Las Vegas. “The fact that he's been able to dominate there is definitely turning some heads.” Long impressed not just on the field, but off of it, too. He was given the Arizona Fall League Community Champion Award for exemplifying “a strong commitment to community service and positive impact beyond the game,” according to a league release. item.title: 'Our gegenpressing was top!' – Jonathan Tah reveals how Germany overwhelmed the Netherlands
item.description: Germany v Netherlands - UEFA Nations League 2026/27 Group A2 MD6 - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich defender Jonathan Tah has praised the squad's energetic gegenpressing and positive mindset following their 5-0 win over the Netherlands. Tah emphasized that the team is firmly focused on building for the future. Solid defensive foundation in Berlin The Bayern Munich centre-back anchored the German backline with authority as Die Nationalmannschaft produced a stunning 5-0 victory over the Netherlands at the Olympiastadion. Working in tandem with a relentless midfield press, Tah helped nullify the Dutch attack to secure a memorable clean sheet. Good mood and lighthearted relief Speaking to the press after the match, Tah revealed that the dressing room was filled with positivity and a well-deserved sense of accomplishment following a hard-fought campaign . "Naturally, it was good and very positive," Tah said regarding the dressing-room mood, adding with a smile that the coach had already outlined playful plans for the break. "The coach was quite exuberant. He joked, 'I now have five months off, and you guys have your next tasks ahead at your clubs.' But no, it was a very positive atmosphere. We were delighted that we could shape the game this way. It wasn't easy. It didn't feel like an easy game right from the start." Looking forward and praising young talent Reflecting on the team's trajectory since the World Cup, Tah stressed the importance of creating positive new moments rather than dwelling on past disappointments. "You keep going through valleys, heights, and depths. Certainly, the World Cup was a low point. But life goes on just the same afterwards. You have to try and succeed in creating positive moments for yourself again. Today was a huge step in the right direction," Tah reflected. He also heaped praise on the younger squad members, adding: "Outstanding job by the young guys. Brajan [Gruda], Derry [Scherhant]... It's not easy. I think Brajan played his second match. Top job, top mentality. You can simply see what quality they possess when you deploy them." The secret behind the performance Concluding his analysis, Tah pointed to the team's tactical execution—specifically their swift recovery of possession—as the decisive factor that prevented the Netherlands from gaining any momentum. "When we win the ball back quickly after losing it, it helps us avoid getting caught in too many transitional situations where we let the opponent grow strong," Tah explained. "We did an outstanding job of that today as well. The gegenpressing was top. That helps us immensely as a team."

item.title: Andorra owner Gerard Pique says Jesus Owono doesn’t deserve ban after footballer’s death
item.description: Andorra owner Gerard Pique believes that goalkeeper Jesus Owono does not deserve the 12-match ban he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel . Owono collided with De Miguel in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier match on 2 November, with De Miguel subsequently rushed to intensive care before passing away the morning after in hospital. Owono, who was sent off for the foul before the match was abandoned, said he was going through “the most difficult days of my life” in the aftermath of De Miguel’s death. He has since been hit with a lengthy suspension for violent conduct by the Spanish football federation (Rfef), with its disciplinary committee saying he used “excessive force” in the collision. Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban after the death of Jesus de Miguel (AP) This has drawn the ire of former Barcelona defender Pique, the majority shareholder of Owono’s club Andorra, who feels the Equatorial Guinea stopper is being punished for the consequences rather than his action. "Players, ​former ⁠players, coaches, goalkeepers, everyone has called it an accident," Pique said in a video posted on social media ⁠late on Monday. “I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened.” Pique says there is inconsistency in the punishment, citing Albacete winger Jose Corpas’ three-match ban after his high challenge on Sabadell midfielder Quadri Liameed left him hospitalised. Gerard Pique is the owner of second-tier club Andorra (AFP/Getty) “Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,” he added. “With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?” Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely. Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again, with Pique stating that Owono will live with the repercussions of the incident for much longer than the duration of his 12-game suspension. “Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to compete,” he said. “No sanction is going to bring [De Miguel] back to us.”

item.description: If last year's Dwyer boys golf team proved that the Panthers' program could be a new hotbed for Palm Beach County talent, this season proved that team success is here to stay. Without both Auburn golfer Hampton Beebe and South Florida golfer Wylie Inman , the Panthers outdid their 2025 roster by three strokes at the Class 3A state championship winning the team's second-straight title with a 584 team score. William Cui paced the entire field with a 139 (5-under) to win the individual crown, guiding a team that made up for its lack in seniority by following the same 'mamba mentality' that head coach Eric Fasone crafted in the wake of basketball legend Kobe Bryant's approach to his game. A look back: How Hampton Beebe, Dwyer boys golf ran away with the Florida 3A state championship "We just stuck with the same recipe, basically," Fasone said. "We just kept grinding throughout the season ― daily practices, lots of team meetings, reflecting after matches, team bonding ― and you know, putting those things together, we just had the same outcome sweeping through districts, then regionals, then having another state title n our hands." Cui, a Georgia Tech commit, sank a putt against the wind on the 18th hole to cement his first-place standing. Beyond Cui and Tankhun "Tank" Ritthisorn, Dwyer's roster was comprised of talented underclassmen, making the state title even more impressive with the pressure on. A number of college coaches were in attendance. "There weren't as many colleges last year as there were this year and the boys see that," Fasone said. "So, it adds another layer of stress on performance. One of my roles was just reminding them to have fun and just remaining positive, and I think that's played a big role in the success story that we have." item.description: In college, Quinn Fordham Gray Sr. never lost the Florida Classic to Bethune-Cookman while playing quarterback at Florida A&M . “When we were on that field of play, we took no prisoners,” Gray told local reporters in Monday’s pregame press conference. “To be able to go into that game every year knowing that you got an opportunity to beat your rival is truly what it’s all about.” Saturday will be a “dream come true” for the first-year FAMU head coach. In the very game he once starred in, Gray will lead the Rattlers into Orlando’s Camping World Stadium to face the B-CU Wildcats. Gray’s return to the Florida Classic as head coach marks another chapter in his FAMU history. After starring as the Rattlers’ quarterback from 1997-2001, Gray returned to the program as an assistant coach from 2011-14. During those four seasons, FAMU was swept by Bethune-Cookman in the annual Classic. The Week 12 Southwestern Athletic Conference regular season finale kicks off at 3:30 p.m. on ESPN+ and on Tallahassee radio station 96.1 JAMZ . The banter has already begun between the FAMU and Bethune fanbases to set the stage for Orlando. But Gray says it’s “business as usual” for his inaugural Rattler team. As fate would have it, Gray will coach against the legendary Wildcats coach Alvin “Shine” Wyatt at the Florida Classic. Bethune-Cookman parted ways with fourth-year head coach Raymond Woodie Jr. last Sunday, Nov. 15, a day after the Wildcats’ third straight loss, a 32-21 home loss to Grambling State. Wyatt is the winningest head coach in Bethune-Cookman football history, spending 1976 to 1996 as an assistant before being promoted to head coach until 2009, overlapping with Gray’s time as a FAMU player. Wyatt hasn’t coached since 2017 following a four-year stint at Edward Waters. “Coach has been away from the sidelines for a good little while,” Gray said of the coaching change. “It’ll be interesting to see what it is he’ll bring to the sidelines.
